open_obligations.what_is_open: An affirmative rational certificate remains open.  Concretely, one must exhibit a finite signed Gaussian mixture with non-collinear rational support and rational effective weights whose Bayes decision probabilities at every charged support point equal the rational numbers forced by complementary slackness, and then certify the continuum of endpoint risks and a curved regular score-zero arc.  Alternatively, one must prove that no such rational mixture can occur in dimension two.
open_obligations.obstruction:
The exact rational requirements impose an arithmetic constraint that interval approximation cannot replace.  Nontrivial sign ambiguity implies \(v>0\).  If a rational certificate had value \(q=v\), then at every positively charged state \((h,+)\) or \((h,-)\), respectively,
\[
 q_{\delta_\pi}(h)=1-\frac{q}{c_+(h)}
 \quad\hbox{or}\quad
 q_{\delta_\pi}(h)=\frac{q}{c_-(h)}.
\]
Because rational affine endpoint data evaluated at rational \(h\) give rational nonzero \(c_+(h)\) and \(c_-(h)\), every displayed Gaussian decision probability must be exactly rational.  The frozen core supplies neither a candidate satisfying these equalities nor a symbolic symmetry that proves them.  A positive-width outward-rounded enclosure can prove a strict inequality, but it cannot by itself prove equality of an analytic Gaussian probability to a prescribed rational number.  Assuming these equalities, or replacing the requested rational support by roots of analytic equations, would assume the crux or violate the target.
open_obligations.attempted:
The prior round reduced the implication from a completed certificate to \(\mathrm{thm:curved-score-no-index-certificate}\).  This round tested the most economical rational unbalanced construction exactly.  Its complete rational primitive table is
\[
\begin{array}{c|l}
\text{object}&\text{rational data}\\ \hline
p&2\\
H&\operatorname{conv}\{(-2,-2),(2,-2),(2,2),(-2,2)\}=[-2,2]^2\\
\Sigma&\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\\
J_-&\{1\},\quad a_1^-=-1,\quad b_1^-=(0,0)^\top\\
J_+&\{1\},\quad a_1^+=3/4,\quad b_1^+=(0,0)^\top
\end{array}
\]
and the complete prior table is
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
h&\text{endpoint sign}&\pi\text{-mass}\\ \hline
(1,0)&+&1/3\\
(-1,0)&+&1/3\\
(0,1)&-&1/6\\
(0,-1)&-&1/6
\end{array}.
\]
Thus \(\ell(h)=-1\) and \(u(h)=3/4\).  All support points lie in \(\operatorname{ri}(H)\), all displayed data are rational, and the endpoint-sign masses are \(2/3\) and \(1/3\).  The game satisfies every member condition of \(\mathcal G_2\): the square is a compact full-dimensional polytope, \(I_2\) is positive definite, \(-1<3/4\), and the interval strictly straddles zero at every \(h\).

Writing \(\varphi=\varphi_{I_2}\), direct completion of squares gives
\[
 A_{\pi,+}(z)=\frac12 e^{-1/2}\varphi(z)\cosh z_1,
 \qquad
 A_{\pi,-}(z)=\frac13 e^{-1/2}\varphi(z)\cosh z_2,
\]
and hence
\[
 B_\pi(z)=e^{-1/2}\varphi(z)
 \left(\frac12\cosh z_1-\frac13\cosh z_2\right).
\]
Thus its Bayes rule has the genuinely non-halfspace boundary
\(3\cosh z_1=2\cosh z_2\).  This candidate nevertheless fails exact saddle closure for a symbolic reason.  Since \(\min(A_{\pi,+},A_{\pi,-})\leq A_{\pi,-}\),
\[
 b(\pi)\leq\int_{\mathbb R^2}A_{\pi,-}(z)\,dz=\frac13.
\]
At \(h=0\), any rule with \(x=q_\delta(0)\) has worst signed risk at least
\[
 \max\left\{\frac34(1-x),x\right\}\geq\frac37.
\]
Consequently \(v\geq3/7>1/3\geq b(\pi)\), so this rational unbalanced curved-score prior is not least favorable and cannot be face-complete.  It is therefore an explicit witness attempt, not a substitute conditional theorem.

Two exact structural checks further delimit the search.  First, if \(h_0\) is the sign-ambiguity point and \(x=q_\delta(h_0)\), then
\[
 \max\{u(h_0)(1-x),[-\ell(h_0)]x\}
 \geq\frac{u(h_0)[-\ell(h_0)]}{u(h_0)-\ell(h_0)}>0,
\]
which proves \(v>0\).  Second, if all support points having nonzero net signed mixture coefficient lie on an affine line \(\bar h+\mathbb R d\), factoring the positive density \(\varphi_\Sigma(z-\bar h)\) from \(B_\pi\) shows that its sign is a function only of \(d^\top\Sigma^{-1}z\).  Its Bayes rule is then one-index.  Hence a curved certificate requires non-collinear effective support; the usual common-reflection device that forces probability \(1/2\) along a single line cannot settle this target.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The strongest closed result is an exact obstruction plus an explicit failed rational candidate.  In any requested certificate, nontrivial sign ambiguity makes \(q=v>0\), complementary slackness makes every charged support risk equal \(q\), and rational primitives therefore force every charged Gaussian treatment probability to be rational through
\(q_{\delta_\pi}(h)=1-q/c_+(h)\) or \(q_{\delta_\pi}(h)=q/c_-(h)\).  Effective support confined to an affine line necessarily gives a one-index Bayes rule, so a successful witness must solve these rational-probability equalities on a non-collinear rational support.  The displayed square example is fully rational, has unequal endpoint-sign masses and the curved analytic boundary \(3\cosh z_1=2\cosh z_2\), but it is ruled out exactly by \(b(\pi)\leq1/3<3/7\leq v\).  No remaining record in the supplied immutable core provides the non-collinear rational equalizer, rational partition, truncation box, directed enclosures, or tail receipts needed to pass from this obstruction to an affirmative certificate or a general impossibility theorem.

prose_updates.tldr: The note solves the unrestricted compact polyhedral Gaussian endpoint game, constructs face-complete least-favorable priors, proves convergence of primal--dual exchange bounds without a complexity-rate claim, and gives a finite sufficient certificate for the no-one-index branch: exact saddle closure for a finite endpoint prior together with a nonvanishing analytic score and one regular curved score-zero arc implies a unique minimax rule outside every measurable one-index class. The asymmetric triangular example has value \(2/3\) and proves coexistence of one-index and non-one-index optima. The requested fully rational unbalanced curved-score witness remains unresolved: an explicit rational attempt has curved boundary \(3\cosh z_1=2\cosh z_2\), but exact inequalities rule it out because \(b(\pi)\leq1/3<3/7\leq v\). The finite all-one-index, coexistence, or no-one-index primitive criterion also remains open. Conditional feasible transfer uses reverse deficiency only for its lower bound and a separate joint total-variation premise for its upper bound; it makes no sample-splitting derivation or rate claim.

project_justification.gap: Theorem 3 of \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local} is the feasible fully differentiable result. Its Assumption 5(i) imposes convexity and centrosymmetry for directionally differentiable bounds, Theorem 4 supplies selected rules for that limit game, Theorem 5 gives their feasible transfer, and the Conclusion leaves the joint directional-differentiability and non-centrosymmetry regime open. \cite{Yata2025Optimal} relies on an antipodal modulus pair. \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision} imposes open-set sign ambiguity and establishes multiplicity without classifying the full unrestricted correspondence; the present primitive class instead uses pointwise sign ambiguity. The remaining gap here is constructive and exact: neither the verified sources nor the frozen core supply a rational unbalanced least-favorable endpoint prior with a globally certified curved Bayes boundary.
project_justification.niche: Finite endpoint priors produce analytic differences of Gaussian mixtures. Their global primal--dual gap and local boundary jets are finite objects that can certify properties of the entire unrestricted minimax correspondence, including failure of every scalar-index representation. Exact rational closure is materially stronger than numerical candidate-prior search because every charged support risk must equal one common value.
project_justification.fill: The project derives unrestricted saddle duality and face-complete dual representatives, proves a convergent exchange certificate without a complexity rate, and proves that exact finite-prior saddle closure plus a nonvanishing curved Bayes-score boundary yields uniqueness and the no-one-index category. It also gives the value-\(2/3\) triangular coexistence regression test. A fully rational unbalanced instance satisfying the curved-score certificate is not claimed: the explicit rational curved attempt recorded this round fails the exact dual lower bound, and the complete primitive trichotomy remains answer-open.

sampling_model.design: The canonical experiment is one observation \(Z_h\sim N(h,\Sigma)\). In the conditional transfer result, the reverse-deficiency condition \(\sup_{h\in H}\lVert L_nN(h,\Sigma)-P_{n,h}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\to0\) is used only for the minimax lower bound. The feasible upper bound is conditional on a separate joint total-variation approximation; no two-sided experiment equivalence is asserted or needed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A training sample may be used to construct \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\), including \(\widehat\Sigma_n\), but legal membership in \(\mathcal G_p\) and the numerical \(\mathsf B_\kappa\) bounds are separate assumptions. On the common legal event, a deterministic measurable tie-breaking premise for the finite-tolerance certified selector is required, and every finite tolerance \(\varepsilon_n\) is strictly positive. The feasible upper bound additionally assumes joint total-variation approximation of \((\widehat Z_n,\widehat{\mathsf G}_n)\) by the Gaussian reference law. Sample splitting is not claimed to derive that premise, and no convergence rate is attached.

prose_updates.related_work: Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye, \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision}, establish multiplicity and qualified failure of linear threshold rules in partially identified treatment choice, but do not exclude every randomized measurable rule based on one linear projection. Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye, \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local}, solve the smooth asymmetric and nonsmooth centrosymmetric regimes separately and leave their joint relaxation open; the present compact asymmetric polyhedral class occupies that orthogonal regime, not a superclass of their full Assumption-5 class. Yata, \cite{Yata2025Optimal}, obtains an optimal one-index rule from an antipodal modulus pair under centrosymmetry. Tetenov, \cite{Tetenov2012Asymmetric}, derives threshold structure for point-identified asymmetric regret, showing that asymmetry alone does not yield the present non-index conclusion. Aradillas Fern\'andez et al., \cite{AradillasFernandezEtAl2025LeastFavorable}, provide a numerical stochastic-mirror-descent method for locating approximate least-favorable distributions and nearly optimal tests; that method can supply candidate priors but does not furnish the exact global rational interval certificate required here. Aradillas Fern\'andez et al., \cite{AradillasFernandezEtAl2025Epsilon}, optimize mixtures over a fixed finite rule menu, whereas the present saddle ranges over all measurable randomized rules. Teicher, \cite{Teicher1963Mixtures}, supplies finite-normal-mixture identifiability, and Zahm et al., \cite{ZahmEtAl2020Ridge}, study measurable ridge functions and gradient diagnostics; neither source proves the exact endpoint-game saddle certificate posed here. Hirano and Porter, \cite{HiranoPorter2009}, provide limit-experiment motivation only; the secondary feasible result is explicitly conditional on reverse deficiency for the lower bound and a separate joint total-variation premise for the upper bound.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The curved-score theorem is a sufficient certificate, not a completed unbalanced example or a necessary-and-sufficient normal-fan classification. Its exact global premise cannot be replaced by a plot, a sampled grid, or a floating-point optimizer gap. With rational primitives and rational \(q\), complementary slackness forces exact rational Gaussian decision probabilities at every charged support point; the current core contains no non-collinear mixture for which those equalities are certified. The value-\(2/3\) triangular witness establishes coexistence only. Exchange iterates use exact restricted-game and worst-state oracles, make no complexity-rate claim, and use strictly positive finite tolerances. Conditional transfer separately assumes reverse deficiency, legal bounded game estimation, selector measurability, and joint total-variation approximation.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved frontier is exact saddle geometry for compact polyhedral Gaussian endpoint games: complete unrestricted duality, face-complete priors, the triangular coexistence witness, convergent primal--dual bounds without a complexity rate, and a finite sufficient curved-score theorem for the no-one-index branch. A rational unbalanced instance satisfying that theorem has not been certified; the explicit rational curved attempt is rejected by the exact gap \(b(\pi)\leq1/3<3/7\leq v\). The full primitive trichotomy remains open. The centered antipodal specialization and the compact-polyhedral overlap with Theorem 4 of \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local} are comparators only. Conditional feasible transfer is secondary, has no named-model instantiation or rate claim, and retains strictly positive finite certificate tolerances.

statement_notes.justification: This remains the early kill test for the no-one-index branch. The explicit rational attempt shows that unbalanced masses and a curved Gaussian-mixture boundary are easy to obtain separately, but exact least-favorability fails and cannot be repaired by numerical precision alone.
statement_notes.gap: The unresolved step is an exact non-collinear rational equalizer: rational saddle value and endpoint data force rational Gaussian decision probabilities at every charged support point, while no verified source or frozen record supplies the required symmetry, interval certificate, or impossibility theorem.
statement_notes.consumer: A successful certificate would prove that genuinely multivariate reporting is sometimes unavoidable; a general impossibility theorem would sharply simplify the classification program. The failed square candidate prevents software from mistaking a curved approximate Bayes boundary for exact minimax closure.

proofs.proof_tex:
Write a second \(p\)-dimensional game as \(\mathsf G'=(H',\Sigma',\ell',u')\), and decorate its objects with primes. For \(x\in[0,1]\), define \(g_+(x)=1-x\) and \(g_-(x)=x\). Thus, by \(\mathrm{def:endpoint-game}\),
\[
 r_{(h,\sigma)}(\delta)=c_{\sigma}(h)
 g_{\sigma}\!\left(E_h\delta(Z_h)\right),
 \qquad \sigma\in\{+,-\}. \tag{1}
\]

We first prove the deterministic perturbation inequality. Suppose \(\mathsf B_{\kappa}(\mathsf G)\) and \(\mathsf B_{\kappa}(\mathsf G')\), and let \(\rho=d_{\mathsf G}(\mathsf G',\mathsf G)\leq(2\kappa)^{-1}\). The bounded-primitive predicate gives \(\lVert h\rVert\leq\kappa\), intercept magnitude at most \(\kappa\), and face-normal norm at most \(\kappa\). Hence every affine endpoint piece has magnitude at most \(\kappa+\kappa^2\) on its domain. A finite maximum or minimum of numbers in that interval remains in the interval, so
\[
 0\leq c_{\sigma}(h)\leq M_{\kappa}:=\kappa(1+\kappa) \tag{2}
\]
for both signs and both games.

Fix \((h',\sigma)\in H'\times\{+,-\}\). By the definition of \(d_{\mathsf G}\), Hausdorff distance between the corresponding endpoint graphs is at most \(\rho\). Therefore there is \(h\in H\) for which
\[
 \lVert h'-h\rVert\leq\rho,
 \qquad
 \lvert c'_{\sigma}(h')-c_{\sigma}(h)\rvert\leq\rho. \tag{3}
\]
For the second inequality, use the matched vertical graph coordinates and the elementary one-Lipschitz inequalities \(\lvert[x]_+-[y]_+\rvert\leq\lvert x-y\rvert\) and \(\lvert[-x]_+-[-y]_+\rvert\leq\lvert x-y\rvert\).

Set
\[
 E=\Sigma^{-1/2}(\Sigma'-\Sigma)\Sigma^{-1/2}.
\]
The covariance part of \(d_{\mathsf G}\) and the lower eigenvalue bound in \(\mathsf B_{\kappa}(\mathsf G)\) imply
\[
 \lVert E\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq\lVert\Sigma^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
       \lVert\Sigma'-\Sigma\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq\kappa\rho\leq\frac12. \tag{4}
\]
Positive definiteness, supplied by membership in \(\mathcal G_p\), makes every inverse and logarithm below well defined. Direct substitution in the Gaussian densities gives
\[
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(N(h',\Sigma')\,\middle\|\,N(h,\Sigma)\right)
 =\frac12\left\{
 \operatorname{tr}E-\log\det(I+E)
 +(h-h')^{\top}\Sigma^{-1}(h-h')
 \right\}. \tag{5}
\]
If \(x\in[-1/2,1/2]\), then \(x-\log(1+x)\leq2x^2\): subtract the left side from \(2x^2\), differentiate, and check its minimum on each side of zero, with equality at zero. Applying this scalar inequality to the eigenvalues of \(E\), and using (3)--(4), yields
\[
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(N(h',\Sigma')\,\middle\|\,N(h,\Sigma)\right)
 \leq \rho^2\left(p\kappa^2+\frac{\kappa}{2}\right). \tag{6}
\]

For completeness, the total-variation inequality needed here follows from convexity. For probability laws \(P\ll Q\), let \(f=dP/dQ\), \(A=\{f\geq1\}\), \(t=P(A)\), and \(s=Q(A)\). Then \(\lVert P-Q\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}=t-s\). Jensen's inequality for \(x\mapsto x\log x\), first under normalized \(Q\) on \(A\) and then on \(A^c\), gives
\[
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P\|Q)
 \geq t\log\frac ts+(1-t)\log\frac{1-t}{1-s}. \tag{7}
\]
The right side, as a function of \(t\) with \(s\) fixed, vanishes with zero first derivative at \(t=s\) and has second derivative \(1/[t(1-t)]\geq4\). Taylor's integral formula therefore bounds it below by \(2(t-s)^2\); boundary cases follow by continuity. Consequently,
\[
 \lVert P-Q\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \leq\sqrt{D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P\|Q)/2}. \tag{8}
\]
Combining (6) and (8),
\[
 \left\lVert N(h',\Sigma')-N(h,\Sigma)\right\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \leq\rho\sqrt{p\kappa^2/2+\kappa/4}. \tag{9}
\]

Because \(0\leq\delta\leq1\), the difference of its expectations under two laws is at most their total-variation distance. Since each \(g_{\sigma}\) is one-Lipschitz and takes values in \([0,1]\), equations (1)--(3) and (9) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \left\lvert r'_{(h',\sigma)}(\delta)-r_{(h,\sigma)}(\delta)\right\rvert
 &\leq \left\lvert c'_{\sigma}(h')-c_{\sigma}(h)\right\rvert
   +M_{\kappa}
   \left\lvert E_{h'}'\delta-E_h\delta\right\rvert\\
 &\leq\rho+M_{\kappa}\rho
 \sqrt{p\kappa^2/2+\kappa/4}
 =\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho). 
 \end{aligned} \tag{10}
\]
Thus \(R'(\delta)\leq R(\delta)+\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho)\). Repeating the graph matching from \(\mathsf G\) to \(\mathsf G'\) gives the reverse inequality. Hence
\[
 \sup_{\delta\in\mathcal D}
 \lvert R'(\delta)-R(\delta)\rvert
 \leq\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho). \tag{11}
\]
Taking infima over the same nonempty rule class \(\mathcal D\) in the two inequalities comprising (11) yields
\[
 \lvert v'-v\rvert\leq\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho). \tag{12}
\]
If \(\rho>(2\kappa)^{-1}\), (2) places both worst-case risks and both values in \([0,M_{\kappa}]\). Therefore (11)--(12) continue to hold with \(\overline\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho)=M_{\kappa}\).

Apply (11)--(12) to \(\mathsf G_{\nu}\). By \(\mathrm{lem:gap-near-optimality}\), the strictly positive finite-tolerance certificate satisfies
\[
 0\leq R_{\nu}(\widetilde\delta_{\nu})-v_{\nu}
 \leq\varepsilon_{\nu}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R(\widetilde\delta_{\nu})-v
 &\leq \lvert R(\widetilde\delta_{\nu})
              -R_{\nu}(\widetilde\delta_{\nu})\rvert
 +(R_{\nu}(\widetilde\delta_{\nu})-v_{\nu})
 +\lvert v_{\nu}-v\rvert\\
 &\leq2\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho_{\nu})+\varepsilon_{\nu}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{13}
\]
No uniqueness, active-face constancy, or indexability property entered (10)--(13), which proves the asserted tie-uniformity.

We next prove the feasible upper bound without using reverse deficiency. The separate legality and boundedness assumptions give, for every \(n\) and \(h\),
\[
 P_{n,h}\!\left(
 \widehat{\mathsf G}_n\in\mathcal G_p,
 \ \mathsf B_{\kappa}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n)
 \right)=1. \tag{14}
\]
The definition of \(Q_{n,h}\) gives equality of the \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\)-marginals,
\[
 \mathcal L_{Q_{n,h}}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n)
 =\mathcal L_{P_{n,h}}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n), \tag{15}
\]
so (14) also holds under \(Q_{n,h}\). By the measurable-selector assumption, the fixed finite-tolerance evaluation map \((G',z)\mapsto d_{G'}(z)\) is Borel measurable on the realized legal games. Its composition with \((\widehat{\mathsf G}_n,\widehat Z_n)\) is therefore measurable under either joint law. Thus all conditional expectations below are defined and \(\widehat\delta_n\) is a feasible rule.

Condition on a realized \(G'=\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\) in (14), write its covariance as \(\Sigma'\), and let \(d_{G'}\) be its certified rule at \(\varepsilon_n>0\). Under \(Q_{n,h}\), conditionally on \(G'\), the signal law is \(N(h,\Sigma')\). Let \(c_{\sigma}\) denote the true-game weight at \(h\). Define the conditional true signed loss by
\[
 \mathcal L^Q_{n,h,\sigma}(G')
 :=c_{\sigma}(h)
 E_{N(h,\Sigma')}\!\left[g_{\sigma}(d_{G'}(Z))\right]. \tag{16}
\]
Let \(\rho'=d_{\mathsf G}(G',\mathsf G)\). Matching the true endpoint graph at \((h,c_{\sigma}(h))\) to the corresponding graph of \(G'\), and repeating (3) and (10) with the common covariance \(\Sigma'\), gives
\[
 \mathcal L^Q_{n,h,\sigma}(G')
 \leq R_{G'}(d_{G'})+overline\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho'). \tag{17}
\]
This use of the extended modulus also covers \(\rho'>(2\kappa)^{-1}\). The gap lemma and (12), again in its extended form, give
\[
 R_{G'}(d_{G'})
 \leq v(G')+\varepsilon_n
 \leq v+\varepsilon_n+overline\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho'). \tag{18}
\]
Combining (17)--(18), averaging under \(Q_{n,h}\), using (15), and then using the definition of \(\alpha_n\), yields
\[
 \sup_{h\in H}\max_{\sigma\in\{+,-\}}
 E_{Q_{n,h}}\!\left[\mathcal L^Q_{n,h,\sigma}
       (\widehat{\mathsf G}_n)\right]
 \leq v+\varepsilon_n+2\alpha_n. \tag{19}
\]
For a fixed \((h,\sigma)\), the realized loss as a function of \((\widehat Z_n,\widehat{\mathsf G}_n)\) is measurable by the selector premise and lies in \([0,M_{\kappa}]\) by (2). The separate joint total-variation assumption and the elementary bounded-function inequality therefore transfer (19) at cost at most \(M_{\kappa}\gamma_n\). Taking the maximum over signs and supremum over \(h\) gives
\[
 \mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{loc}}(\widehat\delta_n)-v
 \leq\varepsilon_n+2\alpha_n+M_{\kappa}\gamma_n. \tag{20}
\]
In particular, neither \(L_n\) nor \(\lambda_n\) has been used in the upper bound.

It remains to prove the lower comparison. Let \(d:\mathcal X_n\to[0,1]\) be any measurable randomized rule, and use the reverse kernel to define
\[
 \delta_d(z)=\int_{\mathcal X_n}d(x)L_n(dx\mid z). \tag{21}
\]
The defining measurability of a Markov kernel makes \(\delta_d\) Borel measurable; its range is contained in \([0,1]\), so its Lebesgue-almost-everywhere class belongs to \(\mathcal D\). Moreover,
\[
 E_{N(h,\Sigma)}\delta_d
 =E_{L_nN(h,\Sigma)}d. \tag{22}
\]
The reverse-deficiency assumption and \(0\leq d\leq1\) imply, uniformly in \(h\),
\[
 \left\lvert E_{L_nN(h,\Sigma)}d-E_{P_{n,h}}d\right\rvert
 \leq\lambda_n. \tag{23}
\]
Define
\[
 r^{\mathrm{orig}}_{n,(h,+)}(d)
 =c_+(h)\{1-E_{P_{n,h}}d\},
 \qquad
 r^{\mathrm{orig}}_{n,(h,-)}(d)
 =c_-(h)E_{P_{n,h}}d.
\]
Equations (2), (22), and (23) show, for every \(s\in S\),
\[
 r_s(\delta_d)
 \leq r^{\mathrm{orig}}_{n,s}(d)+M_{\kappa}\lambda_n. \tag{24}
\]
Taking suprema over \(s\), using the definition of \(\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\), and then using \(v=\inf_{\delta\in\mathcal D}R(\delta)\leq R(\delta_d)\), we obtain
\[
 v\leq R(\delta_d)
 \leq\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{loc}}(d)+M_{\kappa}\lambda_n,
\]
or equivalently
\[
 \mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{loc}}(d)-v\geq-M_{\kappa}\lambda_n. \tag{25}
\]
Apply (25) to the measurable feasible rule \(d=\widehat\delta_n\) and combine it with (20). If the finite tolerances remain strictly positive, \(\varepsilon_n\to0\), and \(\alpha_n+\gamma_n+\lambda_n\to0\), the lower and upper bounds converge to zero, proving \(\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{loc}}(\widehat\delta_n)\to v\). The argument only propagates the displayed approximation errors and makes no rate claim.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Fix \(\kappa\geq 1\). Suppose \(\mathsf G\in\mathcal G_p\), \(\mathsf G_{\nu}\in\mathcal G_p\), \(\mathsf B_{\kappa}(\mathsf G)\), and \(\mathsf B_{\kappa}(\mathsf G_{\nu})\) for every \(\nu\). Put \(\rho_{\nu}=d_{\mathsf G}(\mathsf G_{\nu},\mathsf G)\). Whenever \(\rho_{\nu}\leq(2\kappa)^{-1}\),
\[
 \sup_{\delta\in\mathcal D}\lvert R_{\nu}(\delta)-R(\delta)\rvert
 \leq\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho_{\nu}),
 \qquad
 \lvert v_{\nu}-v\rvert\leq\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho_{\nu}).
\]
Hence a certified \(\widetilde\delta_{\nu}\) computed at a strictly positive tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\nu}>0\) obeys
\[
 R(\widetilde\delta_{\nu})-v
 \leq\varepsilon_{\nu}+2\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho_{\nu}),
\]
including along sequences crossing endpoint-face ties and all three indexability categories.

For feasible transfer, suppose separately that the estimated game is legal and \(\kappa\)-bounded almost surely, that the joint total-variation condition \(\gamma_n\to0\) holds, and that the finite-tolerance certified selector is measurable. Then, for every \(n\) and \(h\in H\), \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\in\mathcal G_p\) and \(\mathsf B_{\kappa}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n)\), \(P_{n,h}\)-almost surely. Moreover,
\[
 \mathcal L_{Q_{n,h}}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n)
 =\mathcal L_{P_{n,h}}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n),
\]
so both properties also hold \(Q_{n,h}\)-almost surely. On this common legal event, run \(\mathrm{def:stable-selector}\) at a strictly positive tolerance \(\varepsilon_n>0\), and put
\[
 \alpha_n=\sup_{h\in H}E_{P_{n,h}}\!\left[
 \overline\omega_{p,\kappa}\!\left(
 d_{\mathsf G}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n,\mathsf G)
 \right)\right].
\]
The resulting measurable feasible rule satisfies the upper bound
\[
 \mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{loc}}(\widehat\delta_n)-v
 \leq\varepsilon_n+2\alpha_n+M_{\kappa}\gamma_n.
\]
Separately, suppose there are \(h\)-independent reverse Markov kernels \(L_n\) such that
\[
 \lambda_n=sup_{h\in H}
 \left\lVert L_nN(h,\Sigma)-P_{n,h}\right\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Then every measurable randomized original-experiment rule \(d:\mathcal X_n\to[0,1]\) satisfies
\[
 \mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{loc}}(d)-v\geq-M_{\kappa}\lambda_n.
\]
In particular, when both sets of conditions hold,
\[
 -M_{\kappa}\lambda_n
 \leq\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{loc}}(\widehat\delta_n)-v
 \leq\varepsilon_n+2\alpha_n+M_{\kappa}\gamma_n.
\]
Consequently, if \(\varepsilon_n>0\) for every finite \(n\), \(\varepsilon_n\to0\), and \(\alpha_n+\gamma_n+\lambda_n\to0\), then \(\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{loc}}(\widehat\delta_n)\to v\). No convergence rate is asserted.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The former feasible claim did not state the measurability needed for a data-dependent certificate selection to define a rule, while its two-sided experiment-equivalence premise contained an unused forward-deficiency condition. proposed.statement:
Fix \(\kappa\geq 1\). Suppose \(\mathsf G\in\mathcal G_p\), \(\mathsf G_{\nu}\in\mathcal G_p\), \(\mathsf B_{\kappa}(\mathsf G)\), and \(\mathsf B_{\kappa}(\mathsf G_{\nu})\) for every \(\nu\). Put \(\rho_{\nu}=d_{\mathsf G}(\mathsf G_{\nu},\mathsf G)\). Whenever \(\rho_{\nu}\leq(2\kappa)^{-1}\),
\[
 \sup_{\delta\in\mathcal D}\lvert R_{\nu}(\delta)-R(\delta)\rvert
 \leq\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho_{\nu}),
 \qquad
 \lvert v_{\nu}-v\rvert\leq\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho_{\nu}).
\]
Hence a certified \(\widetilde\delta_{\nu}\) computed at a strictly positive tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\nu}>0\) obeys
\[
 R(\widetilde\delta_{\nu})-v
 \leq\varepsilon_{\nu}+2\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho_{\nu}),
\]
including along sequences crossing endpoint-face ties and all three indexability categories.

For feasible transfer, suppose separately that the estimated game is legal and \(\kappa\)-bounded almost surely, that the joint total-variation condition \(\gamma_n\to0\) holds, and that the finite-tolerance certified selector is measurable. Then, for every \(n\) and \(h\in H\), \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\in\mathcal G_p\) and \(\mathsf B_{\kappa}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n)\), \(P_{n,h}\)-almost surely. Moreover,
\[
 \mathcal L_{Q_{n,h}}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n)
 =\mathcal L_{P_{n,h}}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n),
\]
so both properties also hold \(Q_{n,h}\)-almost surely. On this common legal event, run \(\mathrm{def:stable-selector}\) at a strictly positive tolerance \(\varepsilon_n>0\), and put
\[
 \alpha_n=\sup_{h\in H}E_{P_{n,h}}\!\left[
 \overline\omega_{p,\kappa}\!\left(
 d_{\mathsf G}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n,\mathsf G)
 \right)\right].
\]
The resulting measurable feasible rule satisfies the upper bound
\[
 \mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{loc}}(\widehat\delta_n)-v
 \leq\varepsilon_n+2\alpha_n+M_{\kappa}\gamma_n.
\]
Separately, suppose there are \(h\)-independent reverse Markov kernels \(L_n\) such that
\[
 \lambda_n=sup_{h\in H}
 \left\lVert L_nN(h,\Sigma)-P_{n,h}\right\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Then every measurable randomized original-experiment rule \(d:\mathcal X_n\to[0,1]\) satisfies
\[
 \mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{loc}}(d)-v\geq-M_{\kappa}\lambda_n.
\]
In particular, when both sets of conditions hold,
\[
 -M_{\kappa}\lambda_n
 \leq\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{loc}}(\widehat\delta_n)-v
 \leq\varepsilon_n+2\alpha_n+M_{\kappa}\gamma_n.
\]
Consequently, if \(\varepsilon_n>0\) for every finite \(n\), \(\varepsilon_n\to0\), and \(\alpha_n+\gamma_n+\lambda_n\to0\), then \(\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{loc}}(\widehat\delta_n)\to v\). No convergence rate is asserted.
proposed.justification: The explicit primitive-game modulus controls values and certified rules uniformly across ties. The feasible upper bound is conditional only on legal bounded game estimation, measurable finite-tolerance selection, and the separate joint total-variation approximation; reverse deficiency supplies only the minimax lower comparison.
proposed.gap: Theorem 3 of \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local} gives a feasible fully differentiable rule, while Assumption 5 and Theorem 5 give feasible transfer for its directionally differentiable centrosymmetric rule. The present proposition treats the defined non-centrosymmetric polyhedral game class conditionally on explicit joint-TV and reverse-deficiency premises, without claiming that pointwise LAN, sample splitting, or primitive model conditions imply those premises and without asserting a rate.
proposed.consumer: Researchers with independently verified joint approximation, reverse deficiency, and a measurable certificate implementation obtain a feasible rule whose regret guarantee remains valid near face and indexability boundaries.
